walkthroughs.body_html:
Energetics — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Energetics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Energetics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which reaction has ΔH = ΔH_f° as defined?
options: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l)
H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) → H₂O(l)
H₂O(l) → H₂(g) + ½O₂(g)
H₂O(g) → H₂O(l)
Positive ΔH
Negative ΔH
ΔH = 0
Variable ΔH

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: Hess's Law works because reactions can only happen in one specific direction.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
Hess's Law works because reactions can only happen in one specific direction.
Hess's Law works because energy always cancels out around any cycle.
Enthalpy is a state function — change depends only on initial and final states, not the route taken.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.

mcqs.q: What are the units of Kc for a reaction?
options: Kc is always dimensionless.
Kc always has units of mol dm^-3.
They depend on Δn (the difference between moles of gaseous/aqueous products and reactants) — Kc can be dimensionless or have units like mol dm^-3.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
